hyps.why: If edge 0 is none, node 1 outputs zeros, so a conv on edge 4 adds no useful computation.
A conv on edge 2 only processes node 1's output, which is zero when edge 0 is none.
Replacing none adds a whole new conv path into the output, a bigger gain than swapping an existing operation.
Removing the direct input-to-output edge usually hurts, but it changes nothing when the edge is already none.
Cutting edge 0 starves the conv on edge 4 of input, removing a valuable conv path.
With edge 1 cut, node 2 depends only on node 1, weakening the conv on edge 5 that feeds the output.
When edge 5 contributes nothing, the output relies more on the direct edge, so a conv there matters more.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with parameter-free pooling loses capacity, while replacing other operations costs little.
Turning on edge 0 with a conv brings node 1 and its downstream edges to life, beyond the conv's own value.
Swapping a conv for an identity on edge 4 reduces depth and capacity, unlike swapping out none or pooling.
